title: BH-01 Phase 5 local browser behavior and DOM vertical-slice gate
command_refs: docker run --rm --network none <pinned-elixir> mix bh01.browser_package --out-dir generated

normalization.subject: cross-run semantic checkpoints
normalization.method: Remove only reviewed wall-clock, opaque process, worker-blob, and lifecycle-cleanup duration variance while preserving order, generation, identity, state, failures, resources, DOM observations, and unexplained output; compare compact JSON bytes by SHA-256.

normalization.subject: browser network identity
normalization.method: Replace each random runtime-worker blob UUID with one typed blob identity and retain the sorted unique profile path inventory plus a separate post-readiness behavior request slice.

normalization.subject: timing and resource observations
normalization.method: Round retained browser timing observations to microsecond precision without using them in semantic equivalence; retain memory pages, known ownership counts, and explicit unknown worker/runtime-inventory fields without inference.

limitations: Only one exact headless Chromium 152/Linux x86-64 environment was executed; all browsers remain unsupported.
Fixture protocols and DOM operations are disposable BH-01 boundaries, not public BlazeX component, tree, renderer, capability, effect, forms, or host APIs.
No authenticated command, Phoenix changeset, LiveView, LocalLiveView, Plug-only composition, server validation, or server-authority behavior is established.
Popcorn 0.3.3 still requires CSP unsafe-eval; no production security disposition exists.
The unpruned AVM has not passed payload, startup, memory, CPU, interaction, reliability, cleanup, accessibility, or mobile budgets.
The parent frame does not expose worker count or runtime-wide process inventory; unavailable observations were not represented as zero.
Accessible role, name, relationship, and keyboard observations were made without assistive technology and do not establish accessibility compliance.
Reverse proxy, CDN, precompression, service worker, production HTTPS, deployment rollback, non-local origins, browser crash recovery, stress, and cross-browser behavior remain unverified.

outcome.summary: Phase 5 local browser behavior and DOM gate passed narrowly; Phase 6 is eligible but not authorized.
outcome.expected: The disposable Elixir fixture proves bounded local state, keyed identity, form input/validation, timer/message, renderer-owned DOM update, accessibility observation, generation replacement, fail-closed negative behavior, no local server round trip, repeatable semantic traces, cleanup convergence, and abstraction isolation in the exact pinned browser without stabilizing BH-02 contracts.
outcome.observed: Two independent Chrome 152 runs produced the same 29-checkpoint trace; local behavior generated no network request; all declared behavior and DOM negatives returned typed failures with atomic rollback; original and generation-2 replacement stops reached zero known owned resources; four proofs received provisional passes; fixture and standalone-DOM leakage guards passed.
